correctness.rationale: For A_d=k[x_1,...,x_d]/(x_i^2), d>=2, the squarefree basis and decomposition A_d=B⊕LB classify all linear-leading principal ideals. In char2 every f in maximal ideal squares to zero by Frobenius; after GL_d normalization, unit multiplication makes a unique generator L+g with g in m_B^2, and automorphism L↦L+g carries Ann(L)=(L) to Ann(L+g)=(L+g). Thus each initial projective line has affine fiber of dimension 2^(d-1)-d and total dimension 2^(d-1)-1. In odd char the degree-2 coefficients of f² force at most one nonzero linear coefficient, and writing f=x_i u+v gives v=0 by 2uv=0, hence exactly d coordinate ideals. For finite q counts are d (odd q) or q^(2^(d-1)-d)*(q^d-1)/(q-1) (even q). Independent complete F2,d=3 ideal enumeration from the multiplication table confirms 14 distinct self-annihilating ideals, each half-dimension. Proof handles arbitrary fields and all d>=2; these are DISTINCT ideals, not automorphism orbits.
